[[2007]] [[Associated Press|AP National Player of the Year]] | tournaments= y | tournament_list = [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]] }} '''Kevin Durant''' (born [[September 29]], [[1988]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{cite web | url = http://www.nbadraft.net/admincp/profiles/kevindurant.html | title = Kevin Durant | accessdate = 2007-03-07 | publisher = NBADraft.net }}{{cite web | url = http://www.texassports.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=16&change_well_id=17&member_id=974 | title = TexasSports.com | accessdate = 2007-03-09}}) is a 6'10" [[college basketball]] player who played for the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in the [[Big 12 Conference]] of the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] during the 2006-2007 season. He was selected as the 2006-2007 [[Phillips 66]] Big 12 Player of the Year and received numerous other awards. After his freshman season, Durant opted to enter the [[2007 NBA Draft|NBA Draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.texassports.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=16&url_article_id=6392&url_subchannel_id=&change_well_id=2 |title=Durant to declare for NBA Draft |publisher=Texas Longhorns Athletics |accessdate=2007-04-15}} == High school == A basketball player from his earliest days, Durant played for a very successful [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] youth basketball team. Durant's team, the [[PG Jaguars]], won multiple national championships and included fellow blue chip recruits [[Michael Beasley]] ([[Kansas State Wildcats|Kansas State]]) and Chris Braswell ([[Georgetown Hoyas basketball|Georgetown]]). Durant later moved on to play AAU ball with fellow McDonald's All American [[Tywon Lawson]] ([[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]) for the DC Blue Devils. During this time Durant also starred for the [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] basketball team, which won the 2005 USA Today National Championship. Durant transferred back home for the 2005-2006 school year to play for Stu Vetter at [[Montrose Christian School]] in [[Rockville, Maryland]]. At Montrose, Durant led the team in scoring and was named 2006 All-Met Player of the Year in Boys' Basketball by ''[[The Washington Post]]''. Durant also was named a McDonald's All American and was co-MVP of the 2006 McDonald's All American game with [[Chase Budinger]]. Coming out of high school, Durant was widely regarded as the second-best high school basketball player from the class of 2006 (behind [[Greg Oden]]).{{cite web | url = http://scout.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&cfg=bb&c=4&pid=88&yr=2006 | title = Basketball Recruiting: Top Recruits | accessdate = 2007-03-07 | publisher = ScoutHoops.com }}{{cite web | url = http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1428 | title = Prospect Ranking: Final Rivals150 Class of 2006 | accessdate = 2007-03-07 | date = 2006-05-02 | publisher = [[Rivals.com]]}} ==College== Durant, a 6' 10" [[small forward]] with a 7'4¾" wingspan[http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2894925 Report: Durant's workout raises eyebrows at camp], updated June 6, 2007, was widely hailed by the media as the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]]'s top freshman and a top candidate for Freshman of the Year.{{cite web | url = http://msn.foxsports.com/cbk/story/5922838 | title = Longhorns' Durant is simply special | accessdate = 2007-03-07 | last = Goodman | first = Jeff | date = 2006-09-01 | format = pdf | publisher = FoxSports.net | archiveurl = http://www.texassports.com/doc_lib/FoxSports.com_--_Longhorns_Durant_is_simply_special.pdf | archivedate = 2006-09-01 }} He averaged 25.8 points per game and 11.1 rebounds a game his freshman year. In Big 12 play he averaged 28.9 points per game and 12.5 rebounds. His college career high for scoring is 37, which he has achieved on four occasions. Durant had twenty 30-point games his freshman year, including a losing effort against [[University of Kansas|Kansas]] for the regular season [[Big 12]] title. In [[March]] [[2007]], Durant was named the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] Division I Player of the Year,{{cite press release | title = Longhorns’ Freshman Durant Named NABC Division I Player of the Year | publisher = [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] | date = March 21, 2007 | url = http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/nabc/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2007DivIPlayeroftheYear.pdf | format = pdf | accessdate = 2007-03-22 }} and received the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]{{cite press release | title = USBWA names Durant, Bennett as player, coach of the year | publisher = [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] | date=[[2007-03-27]] | url= http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2007/robertson070327.html | accessdate = 2007-03-27 }} and the [[Adolph Rupp Trophy|Adolph F. Rupp Trophy]], becoming the first [[college freshman|freshman]] to win each of these awards. On March 30, 2007, he was selected as the Associated Press college player of the year, becoming the first freshman and the first Texas athlete to receive this award since its inception in 1961.{{cite news | first = Chip | last = Brown | title = UT's Durant racking up awards | url = http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/topstories/stories/032807dnspoutdurant.9b69ad4.html | work = [[Dallas Morning News]] | date = [[2007-03-28]] | accessdate = 2007-03-28 | quote = Durant is the first freshman to win the Oscar Robertson Trophy and the Rupp Trophy. }} On [[April 1]], [[2007]] he became the first freshman to receive the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]]{{cite news | first = Chip | last = Brown | title = Durant named NABC player of the year | url = http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/topstories/stories/032207dnspoutbrief.44280fd.html | work = [[Dallas Morning News]] | date = [[2007-03-22]] | accessdate = 2007-03-22 }} and on [[April 7]], 2007, won the [[John R. Wooden Award]]{{cite web | last = Rosner | first = Mark | url = http://www.statesman.com/blogs/content/shared-gen/blogs/austin/longhorns/entries/2007/04/07/durant_receives_wooden_award.html?cxntfid=blogs_bevo_beat | title = Durant receives Wooden Award | accessdate = 2007-04-07 | date = [[2007-04-07]] | work = Bevo Beat | publisher = [[Austin American-Statesman]] }} In late February 2007, Durant received an invitation to the [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA Basketball]] training camp. He is the second freshman to be invited to the camp ([[Greg Oden]] being the other).{{cite news | first = Chris | last = Tomasson | title = Dantley given Hall of Fame support | url = http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nba/article/0,2777,DRMN_23922_5359105,00.html | work = [[Rocky Mountain News]] | date = 2007-02-17 | accessdate = 2007-03-07 | quote = [[Jerry Colangelo|Colangelo]] said he plans to invite University of Texas player Kevin Durant to [[USA Basketball|Team USA]] training camp this summer. On April 10, 2007, Durant decided to leave Texas and declare for the NBA draft. He's leaving after playing 1 year at the University of Texas.}} ==NBA career== ===NBA Draft=== [[Image:DurantMadness.jpg|right|thumb|''NCAA March Madness 2008'']] Durant declared himself eligible for the [[2007 NBA Draft]] on [[April 11]], [[2007]], and most experts currently view him and fellow freshman [[Greg Oden]] as the two players likely to be selected either 1st overall by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] or 2nd by the [[Seattle Supersonics]].{{cite web |url=http://www.texassports.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=16&url_article_id=6392&url_subchannel_id=&change_well_id=2 |title=Durant to declare for NBA Draft |publisher=Texas Longhorns Athletics |accessdate=2007-04-15}} On [[May 25]], [[2007]], Durant signed his first professional contract. His contract was with [[Upper Deck Company|Upper Deck, Co.]]. The company said that Durant will be the focus of their [[2007-08 NBA season|2007-2008]] NBA [[trading card]] line. Other athletes with Upper Deck deals include [[LeBron James]], [[Michael Jordan]], [[Kobe Bryant]] and [[Dwyane Wade]].http://cbs11tv.com/sports/local_story_145095148.html Durant was also announced to be the coverboy of the new [[NCAA March Madness series|NCAA March Madness 2008]] video game by [[EA Sports]].
